question.text: Three members of the House of Medici went on to hold this office in Rome, taking the names Leo X, Clement VII, and Leo XI.
question.answerHtml: Pope [or “the papacy;” or Supreme Pontiff; or Pontifex Maximus; or Bishop of Rome]
question.clue: Julius II was labeled the "warrior" one of these people after he formed the Holy League.

swap.text: Martyrs and people who perform one miracle can receive this recognition, after which they earn the title of "blessed."
swap.clue: By what name is this process, which implies that the recipients are "blessed" by Heaven, called?

question.text: An Armenian ruler with this name known as the "Illuminator" was responsible for converting the Armeniansfrom Zoroastrianism to Christianity. The first pope with this name names a series of "chants" while the thirteenthnames a calendar which replaced the Julian.
question.clue: Those two theologians with this name are from Nyssa and Nazianzus, and are considered "Cappadocian fathers" along with Basil the Great.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Boston college's radical feminist theologian Mary Daly.
swap.text: Boston College was founded by this religious order which follows the Spiritual Exercises of its founder Ignatius of Loyola.
swap.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

question.leadin: Pope Martin V was elected following this ecumenical council, which also condemned Jan Hus as a heretic.
question.text: Name this 15th century council, which ended the Western Schism.
question.clue: Other decisions included the canonization of St. Bridget of Sweden and a voting of special privilege to Emperor Sigismund, who had called this meeting.

swap.leadin: Several Knightly orders were founded in the Middle Ages to fight in the name of Catholicism.
swap.text: Name this Medieval Order, which took part in the Crusades and were forced off the islands of Cyprus and Rhodes by the Ottomans before becoming the Knights of Malta.
swap.clue: This group, founded by the Blessed Gerard, controlled the fortresses of Margat (mar-GAH) and Krak des Chevaliers ("crack" deh sheh-val-YAY) before it was forced from the Holy Land.

question.leadin: FTPE, answer some questions about the papacy in the 14th century.
question.text: From 1309 to 1378, the pope resided in this southern French city, where he was under the influence of the French king and removed from his see in Rome, the theological foundation of his power.
question.clue: Six elections were held in this city's Palais des Papes during a period alternately called the "Babylonian Captivity."

swap.leadin: Answer these questions involving self-proclaimed knights in history.
swap.text: This crusading order became the first multinational corporation in the world after creating branches all across Europe. They were forcibly disbanded by Philip IV who wanted to seize their money.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Templar [accept The Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon or reasonable equivalents]
swap.clue: This organization triumphed at the Battle of Montgisard, while members of this organization captured at the Battle of Hattin were executed by Saladin.

question.text: In 1997 this Polish pope bestowed Romero with the title Servant of God. This pope's reign from 1978 to his death in 2005 is the 3rd longest in history.
question.answerHtml: Pope John Paul II [or Karol Józef Wojtyła; accept JP2; prompt on Pope John Paul]
question.clue: This man made a prison visit to forgive Mehmet Ali Agca, a member of the Grey Wolves who tried to kill him.

swap.text: The victorious confederation at Lepanto, led by Don Juan of Austria, was known by this name due to the participation of the Papal States.
swap.clue: One of the members of a better-known group of this name won an important battle at Guinegate, also known as the Battle of the Spurs, and two year prior it defeated French forces at the battle of Novarra.

question.leadin: It resulted in troops led by Guillaume de Nogaret storming the papal residence at Anagni and holding Boniface VIII captive for three days.
question.text: Name this papal bull issued by Boniface that proclaimed the supremacy of the church over temporal powers.
question.clue: This declaration was preceded by the bull Etsi de statu, which reversed a previous bull issued only a year and a half prior regarding taxing the clergy.

swap.text: The Albigensian Crusade was called by this Pope, who was also instrumental in organizing the Fourth Crusade. He reigned between Celestine III and Honorius III.
swap.clue: During a council called by this Pope, clergymen were forbidden from being involved in trials by ordeal, and Jews were mandated to wear identifying clothing.

question.leadin: This pope praised "African values" such as "community life" in his "Message to Africa," which contained a thinly veiled appeal to aid the Catholics of Igboland in the Biafran War.
question.text: Name this pope who canonized the Uganda martyrs and later visited Kampala in 1969 in the first papal trip to Africa. This pope presided over the end of Vatican II after the death of John XXIII ("the twenty-third").
question.answerHtml: Paul VI [or Paulus VI or Paolo VI; or Giovanni Battista Enrico Antonio Maria Montini; prompt on Paul or Paulus or Paolo]
question.clue: In July, this pope issued the encyclical Humanae vitae, which condemned artificial birth control. In 1968, this pope who closed the Second Vatican Council also beatified the Korean Martyrs.

swap.text: On his flight back from a trip to Rio de Janeiro, Francis affirmed homosexual orientation is not itself a sin. He then considered the example of a gay person seeking God, and asked this question. It's usually rendered as five or six words in English.
swap.answerHtml: “Who am I to judge [him]?” or “Chi sono io per giudicarlo?”

question.leadin: Name some things about the Great Schism that the Christian Church experienced in 1054.
question.text: The schism was started when the Pope and the Patriarch of Constantinople did this action to each other. In the Catholic Church, this action bans someone from participating actively in the liturgy.
question.clue: This practice by which a religious community can suspend one of its members. In Eastern Orthodox, people subjected to this action cannot receive the Eucharist.

swap.text: The addition in question was this clause in the Nicene creed which translates to "from the Father and the Son." In greek, this clause had a literal one iota difference from the Orthodox preferred version.
swap.clue: Much of the discussion at Ferrara-Florence centered upon this Latin phrase, whose presence in the Nicene Creed was rejected by the Eastern Orthodox church. It describes the origin of the Holy Spirit.

question.leadin: Jonathan Magin would surely want you to answer some questions about the First Crusade.
question.text: The whole shebang began when Pope Urban II made his infamous "God wills it!" speech at this 1095 meeting in France, inspiring folks like Adhemar of Le Puy to zip off to the Holy Land.
question.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

swap.text: This unrecognized 1409 council attempted to sort out the Western Schism by deposing both Benedict and Gregory, but fucked up by electing the compromise pope Alexander V.
swap.clue: It was presided over by the Bishop of Palestrina, and came to a climax with a stirring denunciation delivered by Simon de Cramaud, the Patriarch of Alexandria, after which Baldassare Cossa successfully intrigued on behalf of Peter Philarghi.

question.leadin: This term has been used by Martin Luther and several others to describe the Avignon papacy.
question.text: Identify this term which refers to an event that occurred during the reign of Nebuchadnezzar.
question.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

swap.leadin: Their ranks include St. Hippolytus of Rome, Novatian, Anastasius, and Anacletus II, while more notable individuals to hold this dubious distinction include Robert of Geneva and Benedict XIII.
swap.text: Name the position held by all of these individuals, the later two of which resided in Avignon during the Great Western Schism.
swap.clue: Clement VII was the first of two of these popes, who are not considered official by the Roman Catholic Church. Modern groups of them include the Sedevacantist ones and the Conclavist ones.
